evidence: README should document the operator-facing worktree workflow and merge/cleanup conventions.
Proposal creation is the earliest Cartographer stage where a topic can be routed into an isolated branch/worktree.
Plans should preserve worktree assumptions, branch metadata, and merge-readiness validation.
Implementation already owns git preflight, phase commits, and final validation, so it should enforce worktree safety gates.
Indexes are generated per checkout and ignored; topic artifacts are the durable graph/rationale files that merge.
The extension registers deterministic tools; a worktree helper can remain CLI-only initially or be wrapped here later.
A helper script can centralize safe Git worktree commands and make the workflow testable in temporary repositories.
Proposal artifacts are inputs to planning; worktree metadata should carry forward.
Plan phases are implemented by the implement skill; worktree validations should be available before worker handoff.
Implement delegates single-phase edits to pathfinder/worker agents; handoffs need branch/worktree metadata and stop rules.
Auditor can review deterministic receipts for worktree safety and merge readiness after validation.
Temporary git repository patterns in index tests match the project instruction to avoid mutating the real `.plan/` during tests.
Docs tests can assert that proposal, plan, and implement skills document worktree mode and single-writer constraints.
Package scripts define the final quality gates for proposed worktree helper/docs changes.
